_comment: Phase 2 output. PROVISIONAL — read the caveat before trusting it.
caveat: Two technically clean recordings disagree by 12 ms on the lag:
rotation 1  corr 0.882  lag -17.2 ms  (injection recovery +/-0.1 ms)
lag A2      corr 0.842  lag  -5.1 ms  (injection recovery +/-3.4 ms)
The correlation method compares a 10 Hz lidar-derived yaw signal against
ARKit and has hit its noise floor. Smooth periodic sweeps make it worse,
not better: steady tempo produces a narrowband signal whose correlation
peak is broad and poorly localised.
IMPACT: 12 ms at 30 deg/s is 0.36 deg, about 3 cm at 5 m and 1.3 cm at 2 m.
PLAN: use this as an INITIALISATION only. Phase 3 solves the time offset
jointly with the extrinsics, where every lidar return is a constraint
instead of one yaw estimate per revolution. If Phase 3 converges cleanly
the timing was fine; if it stalls, timing is the first suspect.
sign_convention: lag > 0 means lidar arrival stamps are LATE relative to pose times. Verified against a synthetic +40 ms delay. Phase 3 and 4 must use the same convention.
yaw_sign_note: Phase 2's -1 came from correlating angular RATE signals, which only says
whether the two rate curves move together. That is a different question from
the handedness of the C1's angle convention when constructing points, and the
two were conflated. With the mirrored sign no rigid extrinsic can remove the
smear, which made every calibration parameter look unobservable.
Caught by rendering a top-down map: the correct sign shows a clean rectangular
room, the wrong one an unrecognisable blur.
